items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: it was about three years ago we did a record with this very good singer named Anita Gravine

ctx.x: Did any of the Italian melodies or that kind of music creep into your writing?

I guess some of those melodies are so romantic, you know just so flowing and beautiful, yeah. Because the thing is they used to have parties and both families would get together and they’d party for two or three days. And not only play the tunes of the day — you know there was a big Benny Goodman influence at the time, so it was a lot of those kind of tunes, “China Boy” and those things. But also they would play the Italian songs, the ©Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Tarantellas and all of those. So it was there, kind of floating around. It was about three years ago we did a record with this very good singer named Anita Gravine, and it’s called “Jazz in the Italian Cinema.” And we gathered up a bunch of the songs from Italian movies, you know we even used a couple of the melodies from “The Godfather” which were really lovely, from the Fellini movies, a lot of these things — had to have some English lyrics written so we got permission and recorded an album like that.
